articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Debemos dejarnos de excusas y de buscar culpables. Somos un equipo"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la derrota de su equipo, la tercera seguida para abrir la presente edición de la Euroliga
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la derrota de su equipo, la tercera seguida para abrir la presente edición de la Euroliga
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, lamentó la mala primera parte de su equipo ante el Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv, que se impuso al conjunto blanco por 102-98, y reconoció que deben "mejorar", tras firmar el peor arranque en la historia del equipo en la Euroliga. El técnico valoró el gran tercer cuarto de sus jugadores, con el que consiguieron remontar un partido que parecía perdido al descanso, aunque lamentó que las rotaciones no mejorasen al equipo en el tramo final. "Dos partes diferentes. La primera mitad mala defensa y como resultado fue una ofensiva lenta, sin ritmo ni circulación de balón, muy mala. La segunda parte, con mejor agresividad, remontamos, pese a que Hapoel es un equipo muy experimentado, incluso llegamos a ganar por un punto", destavó. "En ese momento necesitamos rotar y los cambios no funcionaron. En el último minuto ellos jugaron inteligente, fueron a la línea de personal y ganaron el partido", añadió en la rueda de prensa posterior al duelo. Cuestionado por qué matices del año pasado del Valencia Basket podría implementar a su actual equipo tras firmar el peor arranque del Real Madrid en la competición (0-3 de balance), Martínez apeló a la unión de sus jugadores y al trabajo y el tiempo para "hacerlo mejor". "De poco vale pensar en el pasado. Ahora estamos en otra realidad. Todo es diferente. Necesitamos trabajar juntos, con la mentalidad de mejorar y necesitamos tiempo para hacerlo mejor. Esto pasa por el día a día, por nuestra mentalidad de entender que la situación no es fácil. Pero no solo es eso. Debemos dejarnos de excusas y dejar de buscar culpables. Somos un equipo en las buenas y en las malas; debemos mejorar", finalizó.

images.caption: Pedro Martínez hace una indicación desde la banda. EFE

articles.title: NBA Insiders Pick Celtics over 76ers as Knicks' Top East Challenger in New Poll from Zach Lowe
articles.summary: While the Philadelphia 76ers built a superteam this offseason by signing LeBron James and acquiring Jaylen Brown, they will have some competition in trying to dethrone the 2026 NBA champion New York Knicks.
articles.body:
While the Philadelphia 76ers built a superteam this offseason by signing LeBron James and acquiring Jaylen Brown, they will have some competition in trying to dethrone the 2026 NBA champion New York Knicks.

NBA insider Zach Lowe said on Thursday's episode of The Zach Lowe Show (5:00 mark) that he polled 30 Eastern Conference coaches and executives on the team besides the Knicks that would most likely represent the East in the 2027 NBA Finals, and they chose the Boston Celtics as the "overwhelming winners of the poll."

"I was actually shocked at the level of optimism for Boston as a Finals team," Lowe said. "... A lot of it was simply based on the fact that they felt safest about Boston, alongside the Knicks, being a top-three seed in the conference when the regular season is over."

Lowe went on to say that there was a three-way tie behind the Celtics between the Sixers, Toronto Raptors and Miami Heat in the poll. The Indiana Pacers finished with the third-most votes.

The Celtics added veterans Paul George and Mitchell Robinson this offseason, the latter of whom defected from the Knicks in free agency. With Jayson Tatum fully recovered from his torn Achilles, he's expected to help lead Boston back to title contention.

It will be exciting to see how things play out when the 2026 NBA season begins later this month, as the East appears deeper than it's ever been with multiple title contenders.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Reacts to LeBron James Saying He Wanted to Help 76ers Star Win NBA Title
articles.summary: New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James has said he wants to be the "final little piece" that helps Joel Embiid win a title and that the big man has "done everything in our league" except win that elusive championship.
articles.body:
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James has said he wants to be the "final little piece" that helps Joel Embiid win a title and that the big man has "done everything in our league" except win that elusive championship.

Embiid appreciated hearing that from the NBA legend.

"You're talking about one of the greatest players to ever play, if not the greatest. To have him say that, in kinda validates—not so much what I've accomplished, but the way my peers think about me," he told ESPN's Malika Andrews (3:30 mark). "I'm at the point in my career where I just want, I need to win. Between everything that's happened, that would be a good ending for the city of Philadelphia and they deserve it."

Expectations are sky-high in Philadelphia after the offseason additions of James and Jaylen Brown. James' has said that a number of factors contributed to his choice of the Sixers in free agency, from Brown's addition to his friendship with Maxey and the team's championship-caliber roster.

But helping Embiid get over the hump also played a part.

"He's done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," he said last week on the Mind the Game podcast. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into The Process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

There are plenty of questions to answer with this new star-studded Philly team as they look to develop chemistry, establish roles and embrace the challenges and sacrifices that naturally come when several star players join forces.

But the main goal on everybody's mind is simple—win a championship.

articles.title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo
articles.summary: Several self-inflicted mistakes have cost the biggest sportswear brand on the planet in recent years.
articles.body:
It's been a difficult few years for Nike.

The largest sportswear brand on the planet, named after the ancient Greek goddess of victory, has been losing of late. Losing sales, losing customers and losing ground to its rivals.

The one-time industry disruptor is now the establishment and in the middle of a tricky turnaround plan aimed at clinging on to market dominance.

Nike's latest financial results show signs a turnaround strategy put in place by company veteran Elliott Hill, who was coaxed out of retirement two years ago to lead the firm, is working - but the pace of change is more marathon than sprint.

However, its recovery has been dented by the loss of football star Kylian Mbappé, who ended his 20-year association with the brand last week to join fast-growing Swiss rival, On.

The Real Madrid striker's departure raises the question of whether Nike can remain the top logo for not just elite athletes, but also the fans that idolise them.

To be clear, Nike is still a mega brand and popular the world over. But missteps have seen hundreds of billions of dollars wiped off its stock market value as its share price tumbled by 75% over five years.

Last month, Nike was ejected from the S&P 100 stock market index of the biggest blue-chip firms in the US.

So what's gone wrong? And can Hill turn things around?

Matt Powell, a veteran analyst and adviser in the sports retail industry, reckons Nike has made "several strategic errors" which have been difficult to reverse, including cutting ties with retailers to sell only direct to customers online and making limited editions items more available.

"The more broadly available those shoes became, the fewer people were interested," Powell says.

Other self-inflicted wounds he suggests include spending research and development cash on digital operations rather than new products.

"They really shut down their innovation on product. Someone jokingly said they were trying to turn Nike into eBay."

That jibe was aimed at John Donahoe, the former eBay boss behind Nike's online direct-to-consumer sales pivot, before he made way for Hill.

Donahoe's four years at Nike coincided with the company's share price plunge.

His tenure saw sales initially soar, driven by pandemic restrictions that boosted online shopping, but subsequent cost-of-living pressures curbed customer spending.

As demand weakened overseas in key markets like China, Nike announced cost cuts and redundancies.

Its digital distraction allowed newer footwear firms on top of the trends to snap at its heels. Shop shelf space previously occupied by Nike was replaced by brands such as On and Hoka.

This was a stark warning to a company that prided and built itself on innovation.

Nike was the firm that signed a deal with a rookie called Michael Jordan in the mid-1980s at a time when the company wasn't a major player in basketball and still mostly known for its running trainers.

The gamble - spending its entire basketball budget on Jordan before he had even competed in the NBA - made Nike what it is today.

The company built a shoe brand around him - Air Jordan. The red and black colours broke NBA rules, but Nike used it as a marketing stunt and paid the fines.

In years that followed Nike partnered with generational talents Tiger Woods, Serena Williams and Cristiano Ronaldo, who all donned the Swoosh on their way to golf, tennis and football greatness.

While the brand retains partnerships with long-retired Jordan, plus Williams and Ronaldo - Woods ended his association in 2024 .

"[I'm] not saying that what they did wasn't great, but it was in the past," said Tim Derdenger, an academic in marketing and strategy. "It's not the future and it's not the current and that is what drives apparel sales today."

Nike's books still boast top athletes, ranging from Rory McIlory to Vinicius Junior.

However, it has now lost its biggest footballing star in Mbappé, who had been with Nike since he was nine years old, along with World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.

Yamal suggested his move to Adidas gave him the chance to stand out from Nike's star-studded roster, while Mbappé said On would see him "surrounded by innovators who dream of the same things I do".

Derdenger suggests Mbappé's move had parallels to Jordan's decision decades earlier to choose Nike over Converse and Adidas due to the opportunity for the athlete to become synonymous with one brand.

"Athletes have egos and those egos want them to be a part of something big and that they're the ones that are helping drive that change, that growth."

Nike boss Hill said the brand has had "some great moments" with Mbappé over two decades.

"We wish him much success as he makes the move," he said during Nike's earnings call, adding that the brand still has a "great stable of athletes".

For all the "doom and gloom", Nike will stay number one, according to Powell - millions worldwide, including young people, remain loyal - but its mistakes have dented its dominance.

"Will Nike be the gorilla they once were? I don't think so. Can the brand come back to growth and profitability? Yes," Powell says.

"When you shut down innovation, you don't turn it back on and it goes right back to full speed," he adds.

Powell thinks Nike's turnaround plan, called "Sport Offense", will start to show positive signs next year.

Hill said Nike had "more work to do" on its sportswear, Jordan brand and in China as the company announced quarterly revenues of $11bn, which undershot analysts' expectations.

Notably, the company cited "headwinds" in China, where revenue declined by 26%.

Sales of its Jordan brand were also down globally. Hill said the firm had been "oversupplying" the iconic retro shoe and will now reduce the volume and frequency of products under the brand.

Nike said it expected revenues to decline by "high-single digits" in the financial year ahead, adding that it planned to make savings of $2.5bn by 2031, some of which will result in job losses.

Nike's chief financial officer Dave Denton said: "Our results are below both our expectations and our potential, and we are focused on closing this gap."

The company's shares fell by more than 8% in extended trading in New York after the earnings were announced.

Last year the company launched a spin-off campaign to its iconic "Just Do It" slogan aimed at younger generations with the line "Why Do It?"

Young people, and future sporting stars, may ask themselves: Why Nike?

Nike boss steps down as company veteran returns

Nike tumbles as upstarts grab market share

articles.title: WNBA veteran Natasha Cloud smears Fever fan with wild domestic abuse claim over pointing finger at A'ja Wilson
articles.summary: Natasha Cloud publicly implied a Fever fan is a domestic abuser after a baseline dustup, despite arena security clearing the spectator of wrongdoing.
articles.body: The WNBA’s favorite narrative — that players are perpetual victims — just reached peak delusion thanks to Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Following Tuesday’s baseline dust-up after a foul on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson confronted a fan, leading Cloud to take to Threads and smear both the Indiana Fever organization and the spectator. Cloud demanded the Fever publicly condemn the fan, despite arena security clearing him of any wrongdoing. League guidelines explicitly prohibit players from stepping off the court or entering spectator space to confront fans. WNBA REFS MISS OPPORTUNITY TO EJECT A'JA WILSON OVER MELTDOWN, ENTERING STANDS Yet, as reported by OutKick’s Dan Zaksheske, the WNBA excused Wilson under the absurd claim that she was standing in a "player escape lane." "[And] imma be the one to say it's time for Indy as an organization to start denouncing some s——t," Cloud posted, defending Wilson and dragging the Fever. Then came the wild leap. Cloud launched slanderous accusations about the spectator’s personal life based on nothing more than a brief clip of him pointing a finger. "Mind you he is the 2nd man to take a step towards the court... Wife had to yank him down out of embarrassment," Cloud wrote. And then she crossed into reckless slander: "Even worse.... if he's willing to do that s——t in public to a woman he doesn't know....how do you think he acts in his home?" THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Sky guard closed her rant by framing players as victims: "No it's not our job to continue to fix the problems. Our job is to hoop & to be safe doing it." A veteran WNBA player publicly implied a fan is a domestic abuser because he pointed a finger after a whistle: pure character assassination. Without a shred of evidence, Cloud casually weaponized domestic violence allegations against a fan who was simply cheering for his home team. This isn't Cloud's first time acting as a courtside moral crusader, either. Just last month, she instigated a baseline scene with former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom in Chicago, marching over to confront him at his seat. In today's WNBA environment, facts are secondary to maintaining the preferred narrative. ENES KANTER FREEDOM SENDS LETTER TO WNBA REQUESTING REVIEW OF SKY EJECTION INCIDENT, FULL TICKET REFUND A vocal contingent of players and media members operates under a bad-faith assumption, labeling Indiana’s fanbase as toxic. You have to ask the obvious question: is this constant outrage really about fan decorum, or is it because Indiana rostered the two most popular white players in the league, Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham? Except the actual facts tell a completely different story. Gainbridge Fieldhouse arena security conducted an immediate, onsite investigation into the baseline incident. Security guards interviewed witnesses, reviewed footage, and officially confirmed that the spectator committed zero violations of the Fan Code of Conduct. He was cleared on the spot and remained in his seat for the rest of Indiana’s playoff win. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Yet for Cloud, official clearance means nothing. The assumption of guilt is permanent because it fits the narrative: Fever fans are bad, players are infallible and standing up to point is dangerous. When a WNBA veteran does it to a fan who was officially cleared of any wrongdoing, the league office stays silent. Protecting the narrative will always come ahead of the truth. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER OutKick reached out to the Indiana Fever for comment and will update this article if a response is provided. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama speaks out against NBA players promoting betting, prediction markets: 'I will never do that'
articles.summary: LeBron James has a Polymarket deal. Giannis Antetokounmpo has a Kalshi deal. Victor Wembanyama has no plans to join them.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has landed a number of high-profile endorsements since making it in the NBA. It appears he has no plans to add betting or prediction market companies to that stable.

Speaking with reporters Thursday, the San Antonio Spurs star was asked if he would consider working with such companies. His answer was an unequivocal no, via Jared Weiss of The Athletic :

"Absolutely not. I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was then asked how he decides which brands to work with. His answer:

"There was a dimension of money in the past. Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not to my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. "Obviously, we earn millions and millions, — this is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

"There was a dimension of money in the past. Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not to my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values.

"Obviously, we earn millions and millions, — this is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

The companies Wembanyama does work with include Nike, Louis Vuitton and Fanatics. He's also the cover athlete of Electronic Arts' "NBA 2K27" this year .

A few high-profile deals between NBA stars and gambling/predictions companies have popped up in recent years. Giannis Antetokounmpo is one of the faces of Kalshi, and also owns a stake in a company that regularly sets up markets covering NBA transactions ( sometimes featuring Antetokounmpo ).

LeBron James , who previously worked with DraftKings, recently inked a deal with Polymarket that will pay him $15 million per year , more than he will make from the Philadelphia 76ers this season. Kevin Durant's Boardroom company has a long-standing deal with Fanduel. Nikola Jokic is an ambassador for Superbet, a company in his native Serbia.

This stuff has not escaped the notice of the NBA. League commissioner Adam Silver was asked about the Kalshi-Antetokounmpo deal in February and said his office was looking into it, via Yahoo Sports' Kelly Iko :

"We currently are looking at prediction markets in the same way as sports betting companies. In the case of Giannis, it's a minuscule investment … We need a better handle on all the activity happening out there."

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement does allow players to endorse and invest in sports betting and prediction markets companies like other businesses, they just can't do anything when it comes to specifically gambling on the NBA.

The introduction of legalized sports betting hasn't been without incident for the NBA, most notably with the arrests of then-Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier and Cleveland Cavaliers assistant coach Damon Jones on federal charges related to NBA bets and the lifetime ban of former Toronto Raptors player Jontay Porter . And that's to say nothing of the harassment and threats its players have received from disgruntled bettors, which the NBA joined other leagues in urging action against last month .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Had Largest Signature Shoe Launch in Nike's History, CEO Says
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoe made history as it was released on Thursday.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoe made history as it was released on Thursday.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill revealed that the Caitlin 1s were launched in 5,000 retail stores, representing the largest signature shoe launch in the company's history.

It also represented twice the average for a Nike Basketball signature shoe, per Hill .

The Caitlin 1s were released in "Caitlin Blue" and yellow "Warning Code" colorways on Thursday. There are also several other colorways of the shoe, which are expected to drop at a later date.

Clark has been with Nike since 2022 and was named a signature athlete by the company in Aug. 2025, which included an eventual shoe.

On June 17, the Caitlin 1s were officially announced .

Clark has remained elite offensively throughout her 2026 campaign with the Fever, averaging 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game on 44.5/36.1/85.2 shooting splits during the regular season.

Through two playoff games this year, she's scored 42 points and dished out 25 assists while pulling down 10 rebounds.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson responds to LeBron James’ recent praise
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson responded to praise from LeBron James and Giannis Antetokounmpo after leading the Knicks to their first title since 1973.
articles.body:
LeBron James' praise for Jalen Brunson carries extra weight after the Knicks' historic 2026 championship run. James revealed he once envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden before New York won the title. He singled out Brunson while explaining his decision to join Philadelphia.

Giannis Antetokounmpo also praised Brunson during his own Miami Heat media availability. Brunson responded with appreciation without treating the attention as an endpoint. His comments fit the mindset that has defined his rise. After leading the Knicks to their first championship since 1973, Brunson enters a new season with league-wide respect and a demanding standard.

LeBron James put Brunson at the center of the Knicks' praise

James' comments came during Philadelphia 76ers media day after he explained that New York had been part of his free-agency thinking. He said he envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden, but the Knicks' championship changed that possibility. James chose Philadelphia and said he was happy there.

Even while discussing that scenario, James praised the team New York had built. He called the Knicks an unbelievable team with unbelievable players and specifically praised Brunson as someone he loves and considers unbelievable. The praise came after Brunson's strongest postseason.

The timing also matters because Philadelphia and New York have recent playoff history. The Knicks swept the 76ers in the 2026 Eastern Conference semifinals, winning all four games by an average margin of 22.3 points. James will now face New York twice this season, including Philadelphia's Oct. 20 opener at Madison Square Garden.

Brunson's response shows how he views the attention

Brunson responded to James and Giannis with appreciation, then returned to improvement. He said he really appreciated the comments and respected the two stars, adding that hearing such recognition was a sign of how much he has grown.

Brunson made clear that praise does not change his approach. He said positive and negative attention both have to go through one ear and out the other because players have to keep becoming better versions of themselves or others will pass them. He acknowledged that he still has a lot of work to do.

That response fits Brunson's approach throughout his rise. His path from a second-round pick to a three-time All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection has been built around preparation, toughness, and consistency rather than the idea that he has reached a finished version of his game.

The championship changed the conversation around Brunson

The 2026 postseason gave Brunson his strongest case for league-wide respect. He averaged 28.4 points during New York's 16-3 playoff run and earned both Eastern Conference Finals MVP and NBA Finals MVP honors as the Knicks captured their first championship since 1973.

Brunson was particularly productive against San Antonio. He averaged 32.6 points, 4.6 assists and 4.2 rebounds across 5 Finals games, then scored 45 points in the title-clinching Game 5. His fourth-quarter scoring helped New York overcome a 16-point deficit in the 94-90 victory.

The shift is visible in what Brunson's postseason accomplishment meant for New York. The Knicks did not simply reach the Finals; they won the title while Brunson became the second player in franchise history to win Finals MVP, joining Willis Reed.

Fun fact: Jalen Brunson graduated from Villanova in just 3 years, earning a degree in communications. He still won 2 NCAA championships during that shortened college career.

Brunson's rise explains why the praise feels different now

Brunson's standing changed dramatically after he arrived in New York in 2022. The Knicks signed him after four seasons with Dallas, but his move created questions about whether he could lead a franchise with championship expectations.

Those questions faded as Brunson took on a larger role. He averaged 24 points in his first season with New York, then made three consecutive All-Star teams while earning three All-NBA selections. The 2026 championship confirmed that progression.

His size remains part of the discussion because the Knicks list him at 6-foot-2. His playoff performances showed how he creates advantages through footwork, pace, strength, and touch around the rim. His Finals run added another layer to a career increasingly defined by late-game production.

Brunson's development also changed how New York's offense was built around him. His ability to handle the ball, create his own shot and make plays late in games gave the Knicks a clear offensive centerpiece as the team progressed toward its championship season.

The Knicks now carry a different standard

The attention from James and Giannis arrives as the Knicks begin their first title defense. New York returns most of the championship core, including Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby, while Mitchell Robinson departed for Boston and Andre Drummond joined the frontcourt.

Brunson's health is also part of the immediate picture. He underwent surgery on his left wrist in July after playing through discomfort during the championship run, but he announced Sept. 24 that he was fully cleared. NBA.com reported that he was ready for training camp.

The schedule connects the season to James. Philadelphia visits Madison Square Garden on Oct. 20, bringing James into the building he once envisioned calling home while Brunson enters his first season as the reigning Finals MVP.

Brunson has framed the next step around continued development rather than outside recognition. His response to James and Giannis captured that balance: appreciation for the respect, followed by an acknowledgment that the work remains unfinished.

LeBron James praised Jalen Brunson and the Knicks after revealing he had once envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden.

Giannis Antetokounmpo also praised Brunson, adding to the recognition surrounding the Knicks star.

Brunson said he appreciates the respect but believes he still has significant work ahead.

Brunson enters the season as the reigning NBA Finals MVP after leading New York to its first championship since 1973.

He has been fully cleared after July wrist surgery and is preparing for the Knicks' title defense.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Defensive Player of the Year win looks like WNBA media rewarding its own hype
articles.summary: Angel Reese earned 46 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year votes, but the Atlanta Dream's unchanged 30-14 record raises some serious questions.
articles.body: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese deserved consideration for the WNBA’s Defensive Player of the Year award. Her rebounding, effort and ability to force turnovers gave voters plenty of reasons to put her in the conversation. Apparently, putting her in the conversation wasn’t enough. Reese received 46 of the 74 votes for the award announced Thursday. Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams finished second with 20. Las Vegas Aces center A’ja Wilson, the best defender in the WNBA as far as I’m concerned, received four. Four. Reese received more than 11 times as many votes as Wilson and more than twice as many as Williams. The result fits a suspicion I’ve had about Reese’s coverage for a long time: too many members of the media want her to be an elite player so badly that they oversell what she actually does. ESPN TURNS ANGEL REESE’S 49 ‘MEBOUNDS’ INTO PROOF THAT SHE’S A LEGENDARY WNBA REBOUNDER An award decided by sportswriters and broadcasters gives them something convenient to point to when anyone questions that assessment. "Of course she’s elite. Look at the award we gave her." Atlanta was already winning 30 games and playing elite defense The Dream finished 30-14 this season. They ranked third in defensive rating, allowing 103.5 points per 100 possessions. A very good season. But how much better did Atlanta get after adding Reese this past offseason? Last year, the Dream finished... 30-14. The exact same record as this season. Surely the team's defense improved by adding the Defensive Player of the Year, right? Well, not exactly. The Dream ranked second in defensive rating, allowing 98.9 points per 100 possessions in 2025. Atlanta already had one of the league’s best defenses before Reese arrived, and the team was actually a little worse defensively this year. That doesn’t mean Reese made Atlanta worse. Rosters change, opponents change and comparing defensive ratings across seasons requires accounting for many variables. But anyone selling her arrival as a dramatic transformation has to explain why the Dream finished with the same number of wins and a slightly worse defensive rating. Reese helped Atlanta allow a league-low 9.5 second-chance points per game, she averaged an impressive 1.8 steals and she led the league in defensive win shares. But she also joined a 30-win team that already played elite defense. A’ja Wilson deserved a lot more than four votes Wilson gives a defense options that Reese doesn’t provide at the same level. She can protect the basket, switch onto a guard and defend a possession that takes her well away from the paint. Against Indiana in August, Wilson guarded Caitlin Clark with the game on the line in overtime and forced the turnover that set up Chelsea Gray’s winning 3-pointer. Aces coach Becky Hammon said after the game: "I’ll take that matchup … any day." I don't think the Atlanta Dream want Reese trying to defend Clark on the perimeter with the game on the line. In fact, if that matchup happened, it would mean some very poor coaching and execution from the Dream. Reese’s activity around the basket is valuable, but Wilson’s ability to handle that assignment is a major reason she's the league's best defender. Wilson led the league in blocks for the fifth consecutive season, averaging 1.9 blocks per game, while Reese averaged just 0.7. Wilson actually averaged more defensive rebounds per game (7.5) than Reese (7.3), while adding 1.4 steals per game. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND The defensive rebounding comparison tends to get lost amid the celebration of Reese’s rebounding records. Of her 521 rebounds this season, 206 came on offense. Those are valuable possessions to create, but they aren’t defensive stops and shouldn't factor into a Defensive Player of the Year conversation. And, of course, there are the "mebounds" Reese gets when she misses a layup and rebounds her own shot. Wilson has advanced statistics supporting her case, too. CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney explained that he voted for Reese while acknowledging that Wilson led the league in defensive VPM, an advanced metric estimating a player’s impact on preventing points. Gabby Williams had a serious argument, too. She regularly took the opponent’s toughest scoring assignment for Golden State’s top-ranked defense. The WNBA’s own awards preview cited Synergy tracking that placed her first in points allowed per possession across tracked play types. Some of the explanations sound a little too eager Consider how Swish Appeal’s Edwin Garcia, an official awards voter, described Reese’s defense. "At the rim, she was a black hole, devouring everything that even attempts to enter the paint," Garcia wrote. He also called her a "shoo-in" for the award. A player averaging fewer than one block per game was supposedly devouring everything near the basket. Protecting the rim involves more than blocking shots, but Garcia’s description makes Reese sound like an overwhelming shot-blocking force. She wasn’t. Garcia also leaned on Atlanta’s defensive on/off numbers, citing a 15.5-point difference with Reese off the floor. CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney used on/off figures, too, but he cited a 13-point gap in his explanation for choosing Reese. Atlanta’s own award announcement said 7.9. That’s an awful lot of confidence in a number that changes considerably depending on where it came from and when it was pulled. And it still measures the performance of five players together, not Reese’s individual defense. ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN Hoops Junkie’s version raises another question. Its defensive on/off comparison puts Aces guard Jackie Young at 15.1 points and A’ja Wilson at 7.0, giving Young a much larger apparent impact on the Aces’ defense. Are we supposed to believe Young is more important to Las Vegas’ defense than Wilson? Watch the Aces play and try making that argument. Young is a good defender, but Wilson is the player protecting the basket, grabbing rebounds and handling assignments most centers couldn’t handle. A number that puts Young so far ahead of Wilson deserves some scrutiny before it becomes the deciding argument for a defensive award. The numbers don’t make Reese the obvious choice SB Nation voter Noa Dalzell cited opponents’ worse shooting numbers with Reese on the floor and wrote: "if Angel Reese is guarding you, your team starts missing shots." Except being on the floor and guarding the shooter are two different things. Reese gets credit in that comparison when a teammate forces a difficult shot or an opponent simply misses an open one. Translating the team’s shooting numbers into a claim about Reese personally shutting down opponents overstates what those numbers establish. Dalzell, like Maloney, acknowledged that Wilson led the league in DVPM and noted that Reese also trailed Gabby Williams and Aliyah Boston in that metric. Two voters openly noted an important individual defensive metric that favored Wilson but decided to push forward using team on/off figures. Unsurprisingly, they leaned more heavily on stats favoring Reese, even if those stats aren't the best barometer for defensive performance. Reese’s on/off advantage is fair game when making her Defensive Player of the Year case. But it doesn’t explain why Wilson barely registered in the voting, or why Williams received fewer than half as many votes as Reese. That’s been my issue with the coverage of Reese for a long time. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD She’s a very good player with limitations that too many people covering her seem determined to overlook. Now, a strong defensive season has become a runaway award victory, and the same media that handed her the trophy can point to it as proof that their assessment was right. It’s a vicious little cycle of self-validation. Reese deserved consideration. But 46 votes to Williams’ 20 and Wilson’s four looks like a media corps that was awfully eager to give itself something to celebrate.

articles.title: 1 Heat player in danger of losing starting job in 2026-27 training camp
articles.summary: No NBA team will add a bigger and better piece to their starting lineup this upcoming season than the Miami Heat. Of course, that is because the team traded...
articles.body:
No NBA team will add a bigger and better piece to their starting lineup this upcoming season than the Miami Heat . Of course, that is because the team traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo, one of the very best players in the NBA . Adding the Greek Freak cost them Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakucionis, and a surplus of draft picks.

The former of those departures was not just a starter for the Heat, but an All-Star. The latter three all had experience starting or potential to start in the near future, had it not been for the blockbuster. The point is, the Heat are going to look a whole lot different this season when it comes to their starting lineup. Antetokounmpo joins Bam Adebayo, a fellow megastar who had an 83-point game last season. The Heat will also likely start Andrew Wiggins and Davion Mitchell. The former number one overall pick never quite lived up to his potential, but he has made a productive career for himself. Mitchell is a defensive-minded, pesky player.

As of now, it appears that the fifth starting spot will go to Klay Thompson , another offseason acquisition. However, Thompson's starting spot is at risk.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Who could take Klay Thompson's starting spot?

Klay Thompson is one of the greatest 3-point shooters in NBA history . His 2,899 long ball makes are the fourth most in NBA history. Of course, Thompson's picture-perfect form and catch-and-shoot mastery was at its best when he was one half of the Splash Brothers. Although Thompson has regressed in recent years, it can even be argued that his 3-point shooting has become underrated.

Thompson really is a perfect fit in Miami's starting five because the Heat desperately needed spacing. Antetokounmpo is a downhill player who wants to dominate the painted area, and while Adebayo's 83-point explosion proved he can score outside, he is still an interior player first and foremost. Both players will draw a lot of attention and kick out to an open Thompson. However, it isn't a guarantee that Thompson actually gets the nod as the starting shooting guard.

Tim Hardaway Jr. also has a case to be in the starting five. Hardaway provides loads of beyond the arc shooting, just like Thompson. However, he is a better scorer from the other two levels at this point in their careers. Hardaway can create his own shot, and his defense actually looked improved with the Denver Nuggets last season.

While the Heat have players who get downhill, they actually lack pure playmakers. Miami might be better off with Hardaway's self-creation ability over Thompson's style of player, which relies on few dribbles and receiving plenty of passes.

Most likely, Thompson will, in fact, be a part of the starting lineup. His regression was highlighted buy a recent buyout by the Dallas Mavericks, though, and if the Washington State product doesn't look like his old self, a team in their contention window like the Heat might consider all possibilities, including having Thompson come off the bench.

articles.body:
There is ample star power in the Fever and Aces' first-round series. It was only right the tilt would go to a decisive third game.

Indiana overcame a dour showing in Game 1 to capture a momentous win in Game 2, emerging as 99-89 victors following another Caitlin Clark masterpiece. The Fever phenom will look to recreate her heroics in the final game of the series; in Game 2, she posted the first-ever 25-point, 15-assist game in league history.

She should get all she could handle in the form of Las Vegas and its talismanic presence in the paint, A'ja Wilson. The presumptive WNBA MVP fell short of her heroics in Game 1. And yet, she looks in ideal position to author a memorable display in the series finale. If she does, it's hard to imagine a scenario where Becky Hammon's side won't succeed.

articles.title: WNBA playoffs live updates, Fever-Aces score: Caitlin Clark, A'ja Wilson face off in Game 3 with trip to semifinals on the line
articles.summary: The WNBA playoffs continue with a winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday night.
articles.body: It all comes down to this for the Indiana Fever and Las Vegas Aces. After A'ja Wilson and the Aces dominated in Game 1, Caitlin Clark led the Fever to a fiery Game 2 win to avoid elimination and send the series back to Vegas. While the Aces have home-court advantage as the higher seed, head coach Becky Hammon said Game 3 "might as well be on the street … Anything can happen in those game scenarios."Last season, this matchup in the semifinals went to overtime of Game 5 before the Aces closed it out and rolled to another championship. Will the Fever be able to write a different story this year with a healthy Clark in tow? We'll find out soon enough, with a trip to the semifinals on the line.
